scripts.build: bun run typecheck:api && bun test && vite build
scripts.//verify:db: Ops check, needs DATABASE_URL. Asserts the unique indexes exist and no duplicate/impossible-score rows are present. Add --race <url> to fire concurrent writes at a live server and prove the upserts hold. Run after any change to answer persistence, grading, or schema — and after provisioning or restoring a database.
scripts.//verify:camera-block: Ops check, needs a SEEDED THROWAWAY database (never production - it starts a real attempt), a built dist and a server on :3100. Drives a real Chromium through login, brief and preflight into a running exam, then blocks the camera the way Chromium does (permission denied + getUserMedia rejecting NotAllowedError + the live track ended) and asserts the hard-stop popup: blocked title, kiosk-true steps, NO countdown, no dismiss, exam unclickable underneath, timer still running, one camera_blocked event, and self-clearing on regrant. Run after ANY change to the camera, lock or proctoring paths - none of this is reachable from a unit test, and the scenario it covers already regressed once.
scripts.//verify:monitor-camera-block: Ops check, same setup as verify:camera-block (SEEDED THROWAWAY database - it starts a real attempt). Proves the OTHER half of the camera block: that it reaches the invigilator. Blocks a candidate's camera, then signs in as the tenant admin and asserts the Live Monitor counts it as a violation, shows the flag on the row, and renders 'Camera access blocked' in red in the drawer with the permission-denied detail. Needed because the drawer loads evidence from the REPORTS endpoint, not from /api/monitor, so the label can be correct while the data never arrives. Re-seed between runs: a leftover in_progress attempt turns the student's Start button into Resume.
scripts.//verify:camera-covered: Ops check, same setup as verify:camera-block (SEEDED THROWAWAY database - it starts a real attempt). Covers the OTHER camera failure: the camera is healthy and delivering frames, but the lens is taped/covered, so only the picture can tell. Fakes a black frame at the getImageData boundary and asserts the 2-minute hard lock: overlay within ~30s, visible countdown, NO dismiss control, uncovering early does NOT release, the full period is served then released, and still-covered at expiry starts another period. SLOW (~6 min) on purpose - the lock is two real minutes and the code holds no test hook to shorten it, because anything the test can call from the page a candidate can call from a console. Re-seed between runs.
scripts.//verify:camera-episode: Ops check, same setup as verify:camera-block (SEEDED THROWAWAY database - it starts a real attempt). Covers the THIRD camera failure: a webcam that can be opened but dies a moment later. Run `python3 scripts/verify-camera-episode.py --prepare` after seeding to shorten the lock to 15s, then this. Fakes the fault at getUserMedia (real stream, video track stopped 700ms later, readyState 'ended' - the exact signal 42 of the 43 real rows carried) and asserts ONE camera_lost row across several lock/re-open cycles, with camera_restored counts proving the failure really did recur, plus a genuinely new failure after a real recovery still getting its own row. Takes ~3 min. Run after ANY change to engageLock, the unlock poll, camera-episode.ts or the camera-health feeder.
scripts.//verify:scale: Ops check, needs a SEEDED THROWAWAY database (never production - it starts a real attempt and writes answers/events), a built dist and a server on :3100. Proves the hot student endpoints still behave AND that they cost few database round trips: heartbeat 1 statement (was 3), autosave 4 (was 7, or 13 for a batch of 7), status 3 (was 6), plus event dedupe on resend, the option-order round trip through the cached question set, the heartbeat reaching the Live Monitor, and both performance indexes created at boot. Budgets are asserted, so a future change that puts a per-request read back on these paths fails here instead of failing an exam hall. Set VERIFY_BASE to measure another build.
scripts.//loadtest: Load generator, LOCAL ONLY (it refuses a non-local base). Seeds N students + running attempts straight into the throwaway SQLite file, mints real HMAC student tokens, and drives the exact client cadence (heartbeat 15s, autosave 20s, events 30s, snapshot 27s). Reports req/s, per-endpoint p50/p95/p99, errors, and what one cold page load actually transfers. Use it before and after any change to the student request paths: `python3 scripts/loadtest-exam.py --students 1000 --seconds 60`.
scripts.//mutate:scale: Mutation test for static-assets.ts and ttl-cache.ts (the scale fix). 37 mutants, every one must be killed. Run after touching either module or its tests - a passing suite over broken source proves nothing.
scripts.//verify:option-order: Ops check, needs DATABASE_URL and a running server. Creates a throwaway exam from real MCQs, answers it by option TEXT as a real student over HTTP, and requires 100%. Run after ANY change to the bundle, autosave, submit, resume or review paths — the option permutation is display-only and a single inverted mapping would score every correct answer zero. Add --base <url> to hit a deployed server.
scripts.//typecheck: Root tsconfig.json is `files: []` + project references, so a bare `tsc --noEmit` type-checks NOTHING. It exited 0 while two undefined identifiers (retryCounts, gradeSubjective) were live in production. Always point tsc at a real project.
